holidays.name: National Hug Your Dog Day
holidays.description: Today your dog gets extra snuggles, whether it's a big bear hug for the Labrador or a gentle squeeze for the chihuahua. It's a day for belly rubs, ear scratches and a few more treats than usual.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on the pet-lover calendar.
holidays.funFact: Not every dog loves a hug. Many dogs prefer a cuddle on the couch or a good chest scratch, so watch for a wagging tail and relaxed ears.

holidays.name: National Siblings Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the brothers and sisters who know your most embarrassing childhood stories. Call, text or send a goofy throwback photo to the people who shared your bunk beds, backseats and bathroom schedules.
holidays.origin: Claudia Evart founded the day in the 1990s to honor her late brother and sister. She chose April 10 because it was her sister Lisette's birthday. It has been celebrated across the U.S. ever since.
holidays.funFact: Evart's Siblings Day Foundation has long campaigned for the day to get official national recognition. Even without it, the day is widely celebrated every year.

holidays.name: National Farm Animals Day
holidays.description: This day is a salute to the cows, pigs, chickens, goats, sheep and horses that live and work on farms. It's a good excuse to visit a petting zoo, learn where your food comes from, or just appreciate a very photogenic goat.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance created by animal-welfare advocates. They wanted people to think about the lives and care of farm animals.
holidays.funFact: Chickens outnumber people on Earth by more than 3 to 1. They are among the most numerous farm animals in the world.
